slides.texte_overlay:
Classic gentleman
skills people always
remember you for
Giving a proper toast. Stand up, raise your glass, three sentences about the person, then sit down. Short, warm and sincere. People remember a good toast for years.
Introducing yourself with your full name. "Hi, I'm Daniel Moreau." Firm handshake, eye contact. It sounds old fashioned, and that's exactly why it stands out today.
Offering your jacket when it gets cold. A small, simple gesture without making a show of it. Kindness done quietly is the very heart of being a real gentleman.
Walking someone home or waiting until they're safely inside. Especially late at night. Making sure people get home safe is one of the kindest habits there is.
Sending a handwritten thank-you after a dinner. Two lines on a card. Almost nobody does it anymore, which is why the people who receive one never forget it.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A gentleman who knows the story behind things always has something worth saying at the table.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A gentleman always has something worth saying.

slides.texte_overlay: Standing up when someone arrives at the table. A tiny sign of respect that says "you matter." It takes a second, and people remember how it made them feel.
